messages:
sam: Flux drift detector just fired for prod/gpu-nodepool :eyes:
sam: It says node_pool.autoscaler.min_size is 5 in the cluster, but our terraform declares 3. Cost spike showing in last 2 hours.
ops-bot: [alert] drift:detection - resource=google_container_node_pool/gpu-nodepool - field=autoscaling.min_node_count - actual=5 expected=3
julia: ouch. Any idea what changed? Did someone manually scale?
devin: I saw a manual `gcloud` resize earlier to handle a training burst, forgot to update TF. Likely that.
aria: Can we reconcile via GitOps (Argo) or do we need a terraform apply?
sam: We should fix Terraform state so infra-as-code is source of truth. Quick options: 1) update TF to match actual (5) and commit, or 2) roll cluster back to declared (3) via `terraform apply` - but that might evict running GPU jobs.
julia: We need to avoid killing customer jobs. What's the active GPU job list? @devin can you check?
devin: Running: `kubectl -n training get pods -l app=trainer -o wide` -> 6 pods on gpu-nodepool. If we drop to 3 nodes some pods will Pending.
sre-lead: Priority is customer jobs + cost. Recommend: pin current capacity, add a Terraform comment referencing the manual resize, and add automated reconciliation that requires a canary window before scaling down.
aria: Agree. Could we create a reconcile action in the GitOps pipeline that opens a PR instead of applying, with an optional `force-apply` for emergencies? That prevents surprise reverts.
sam: Example quick patch for TF to bump expected min nodes and record reason:```hcl
resource "google_container_node_pool" "gpu-nodepool" {
  name       = "gpu-nodepool"
  autoscaling {
    min_node_count = 5 # bumped 2026-03-xx manual resize for training burst - TODO: review
    max_node_count = 20
  }
}
```
julia: Add a jira ticket to revert once training finishes or move jobs to a burst pool. Also add a policy check to prevent manual cloud console resizes without tagging a change-id.
devin: I'll open a ticket: INF-4823 "Manual GPU nodepool resize recorded; reconcile TF" and attach the gcloud command + reasoning.
sre-lead: For longer term: we should add a drift-remediation playbook: detect -> create PR in infra repo with `terraform import` if needed -> run plan in CI -> require 24h approval for scale downs that affect GPU nodes.
aria: Could we automate detection threshold so only >1 node diffs trigger alerts? This one was 2 nodes but spiked cost.
sam: ops-bot, can you add an alert rule tweak request in #eng-infra-alerts?
ops-bot: Request created: alert-rule-change/1782345601 - threshold updated candidate: diff>1 -> pending review by oncall.
julia: Also check taints: if nodes were added without `gpu: true` taint we might have scheduled non-gpu workloads earlier. Anyone check node labels?
devin: `kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=gpu-nodepool -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.spec.taints}\n'` shows the taint present. No stray scheduling.
sam: Next steps agreed: (1) devin create INF-4823 and attach logs (2) julia push TF bump + comment (3) aria draft GitOps PR workflow change to open PRs instead of direct applies for autoscaler changes (4) sre-lead draft playbook for gated scale-downs.
aria: I'll start the PR draft and include a test that runs a plan and flags node_count reductions.
sre-lead: After PRs are in place, we should run a dry-run revert in staging to validate the gating.
julia: Thanks all. One more: add an evaluation job to Redwood Optimize to flag cost regression when GPU node counts increase >10% week-over-week.
sam: noted. Closing thread once PRs and ticket exist. :thumbsup:
